exposure: corrective policy of replacing preoperative type and hold step with blood transfusion request (BTR) hold
Before and after implementation of the corrective policy (replacing preoperative type and hold with BTR hold)
cohort: 1200 blood transfusion requests (BTRs) from patients undergoing elective cesarean sections in a maternity hospital
finding: Replacing the preoperative type and hold policy with a blood transfusion request (BTR) hold policy for healthy patients undergoing elective cesarean sections significantly reduced the crossmatch/transfusion ratio, enhanced the cost-effectiveness of erythrocyte transfusion, and decreased the number of destroyed blood units.
